problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(4,-2,7)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $r\cdot ⟨-3,2,3⟩=27.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Shortest Distance Between a Plane and a Point

feedback.problem: Given that $Q(1,3,4)$ lies on the plane $Π:r\cdot ⟨-4,2,0⟩=2$, find the shortest distance from $P(5,-2,3)$ to $Π.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,3,4⟩-⟨5,-2,3⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,5,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of the plane, we get the normal vector $n=⟨-4,2,0⟩.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|(-4)\cdot (-4)+5\cdot 2+1\cdot 0|}{\sqrt{(-4)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|16+10+0|}{\sqrt{16+4+0}} \\  & =\frac{|26|}{\sqrt{20}} \\  & =\frac{13\sqrt{5}}{5}\end{aligned}
$$
